title: Design and Fabrication of an Elastomeric Unit for Soft Modular Robots in Minimally Invasive Surgery
protocol: Weigh 12 g of part A and 12 g of part B in the same plastic glass or Petri dish.
Mix the weighed parts together, stirring.
Place the mixed silicone materials in a degasser machine under 1 bar vacuum pressure.
Keep the materials under vacuum until all bubbles are removed from the silicone material.
Restore atmospheric pressure into the machine once bubbles are removed and use the silicone.
Pour the silicone inside the assembled mold up to the edge of the shells.
Place the mold in an oven at 60 °C for about 30 min.
Remove the external shells and cap_A.
Insert the cylinders from the bases of the chambers and the stiffening cylinder inside cap_B.
Close the shells again around the module, sliding them 10 mm upward to have a gap of 10 mm between the top surface of the module and the edges of the shells.
Pour the silicone inside the rearranged mold up to the edge of the shells on the top side (including up to the stiffening cylinder).
Put the mold into an oven at 60 °C for about 30 min.
Remove the external shells, cap_B, and the chambers (except the stiffening cylinder).
Cut 3 tubes to the same desired length.
Put silicone glue around one end of each tube for 10 mm without obstructing the tubes.
Insert the tubes inside the 2 mm dedicated channels in the silicone unit.
Allow a curing time of 12 min at room temperature or put the module inside an oven at a higher temperature (50° - 60°) to speed up the drying process.
Cut 700 mm of an expandable braided sheath (about 15 times the height of the module).
Insert a metallic cylinder of 30 mm in diameter and 250 mm in length inside the sheath.
Push down and force the sheath over the cylinder to create crimps.
Fix the sheath in place with a clamp.
Heat the sheath with a heating gun at 350 °C for 2-3 min until it deforms permanently.
Allow the sheath to cool down.
Remove the internal cylinder.
Pass tubes through the holes of cap_C.
Pour 3 g of silicone into cap_C.
Clamp cap_C to a support higher than the work plane.
Insert the bottom side of the module previously fabricated into cap_C.
Slide the crimped sheath around the module.
Push the first crimps of the sheath inside cap_C and dip them into the freshly poured silicone.
Put the mold into an oven at 60 °C for about 20 min.
Repeat points from passing tubes through holes to putting the mold in the oven for fixing the sheath at the top side using cap_D.
Remove cap_C and cap_D after silicone curing.
Remove the central cylinder.
Pour 5 g of liquid latex into a plastic glass.
Immerse the cylinder for the membrane inside the liquid latex until the surface is completely covered.
Let it dry under a hood for 20 min.
Repeat points from pouring liquid latex to letting it dry under a hood.
Remove the membrane from the mold after drying.
Cut a tube (2 mm in diameter) to the desired length (300 mm, for example).
Cut a squared piece of about 100 mm² of nylon tissue.
Close one end of the tube with the nylon tissue using a plastic paraffin film or superglue.
Weigh 4 g of coffee powder and fill the membrane with it.
Insert the tube into the filled membrane, fixing it around the tube using a plastic paraffin film.
Apply a vacuum on the other side of the tube to stiffen the membrane.
Insert the stiffened membrane inside the empty central channel of the siliconic module.
Glue the ends of the stiffening membrane to the silicone module.
Close the rings around the top side of the module.
Pour 2 g of silicone into the rings to level the surface.
Let the silicone dry under a hood or in an oven at 60°C.
Remove the rings after drying.
Repeat from cutting a squared piece of about 100 mm² of nylon tissue for the bottom side.
